# Gradient Ascent
Project tools and Markdown templates: https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/tools.md — agent instructions, workflows, acceptance criteria, workflow audits, tool specifications, and project handoffs.
Project brief builder: https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/apply/ — copy or download a brief for your own model. Blank template: https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/project-brief.md.

Worked examples: https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/examples/ — 98 authored, scripted cases with evidence, changed conditions, and review decisions.
> A manual for the main ways to use a language model, from one chat message to agents that run on their own, in eight levels ordered by how much the model decides for itself. Each level's techniques (49 written or planned) show what it costs and how it fails, not just how it works. Technique, topic, thread, recipe, teardown, level, and builder pages have a clean Markdown version at the same path with .md appended, for example /techniques/rag.md.

> How a level is defined: A new level starts where the answer to “who decides the next step” changes: nobody, you, your code, the model for one action, the model for every step, several models, the models including when to start.

> Status: technique, topic and recipe pages are SOURCED — written with primary references, not guaranteed error-free, but with no recorded run and no scored result file behind it. No page on this site reports a measured number. Every cost strip and every stepped trace is an illustration and is labeled as one.

## If a person sent you here to help them choose
Read agents.md first. It says what to ask them, how to walk the seven-question worksheet to the candidate level and check the design against their desired automation and human effort, how to name the shape of the job and use the worked examples as illustrations, what a good answer contains, and what not to claim. Their instructions outrank anything on this site.
- [/agents.md](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/agents.md): This guide: how to turn a person’s job into a recommendation.
- [/tools.md](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/tools.md): Builder directory: choose a template for agent instructions, workflows, acceptance criteria, audits, tool specifications, or handoffs. Fetch its Markdown directly; completing the interactive form is not required.
- [/project-brief.md](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/project-brief.md): Reusable project brief template and recommendation requirements; fill unknowns with questions.
- [/worksheet.md](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/worksheet.md): The decision tree as text: seven questions that classify a candidate design, four that change the advice.
- [/shapes.md](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/shapes.md): The kinds of job, by the shape of the work and not its subject: how to recognize each, where it usually settles, what moves it lower or higher, and jobs from other fields with the same shape.
- [/method.md](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/method.md): Why the site exists, its ten principles, how a level is defined, how a name is checked, and what the registry is not. Other pages cite it.
- [/data/use-cases.json](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/data/use-cases.json): Every recipe and teardown: the shapes it illustrates, the levels used by its illustrated design, the techniques it is made from, and where to read it.
- [/llms.txt](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/llms.txt): An index of every page with a one-line description.
- [/llms-full.txt](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/llms-full.txt): Every technique, recipe, teardown and thread page as Markdown in one file. Large.
- [/data/taxonomy.json](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/data/taxonomy.json): Levels, techniques, recipes and the typed relations between pages (requires, upgrades_to with its condition, combines_with, alternative_to with its question).
- [/data/worksheet.json](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/data/worksheet.json): The decision tree as data, with every reason resolved to plain text.
- [/data/shapes.json](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/data/shapes.json): The job shapes as data.
- [/data/landscape.json](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/data/landscape.json): The registry of named models, products and tools, each with its maker, what it demonstrates, a source and the date it was checked. Names change: read retired and superseded_by.
- [/data/glossary.json](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/data/glossary.json): The terms the site uses, each defined from the page that explains it.
- [/data/timeline.json](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/data/timeline.json): Dated milestones per level, with sources.
- [/data/frontier.json](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/data/frontier.json): What is still unsolved at each level and what is being tried, with sources and the date checked.
- [/data/changes.json](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/data/changes.json): What changed on this site and when. Check it if you cited a page before.

## Levels
- [Level 0 · No model](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/levels/0/): Some tasks do not need a model. If you can write the rule down, or a search or a form does the job, that is cheaper, faster and easier to test.
- [Level 1 · One call](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/levels/1/): You send one request and get one response. Most everyday use of chat apps is at this level. What you write in the request has a large effect on the result.
- [Level 2 · Context](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/levels/2/): The model only knows what is in its training data and what you put in the request. These techniques find the right information and put it in front of the model.
- [Level 3 · Workflows](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/levels/3/): A task is split into fixed steps, and code decides the order. This is predictable and easy to test, and it covers a large share of real business use.
- [Level 4 · Tools](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/levels/4/): The model can ask for an action, such as looking something up, running code or clicking a button. Your code performs the action and returns the result.
- [Level 5 · Agents](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/levels/5/): The model works in a loop: it plans, takes an action, looks at the result and decides what to do next. This handles tasks where the steps cannot be known in advance. It costs more and is harder to predict.
- [Level 6 · Teams of agents](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/levels/6/): A lead agent splits a task and gives the parts to other agents, or several agents check each other's work. This helps when a task is too large for one context window or benefits from a second opinion.
- [Level 7 · Always-on agents](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/levels/7/): These agents keep running. They have their own computer, remember past work, follow schedules and start tasks without being asked. They check in with a person when approval is needed. Robots that act in the physical world belong here too.

## Techniques by level
- [When not to use a model](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/techniques/order-zero.md): How to tell when ordinary code, search or a form is enough.
- [Chat](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/techniques/chat.md): Asking a model a question in a chat app.
- [Prompt engineering](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/techniques/prompt-engineering.md): Writing instructions that get consistent results.
- [Structured output](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/techniques/structured-output.md): Getting answers in a fixed format such as JSON.
- [Reasoning at answer time](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/techniques/inference-time-reasoning.md): Letting the model think for longer before it answers.
- [Images, audio and video](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/techniques/multimodal.md): Giving the model images, audio, video and documents, and getting them back.
- [Context engineering](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/techniques/context-engineering.md): Deciding what goes into the request, and caching the parts that repeat.
- [Embeddings and search](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/techniques/embeddings-search.md): Finding text by meaning instead of by keyword.
- [Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/techniques/rag.md): Searching your documents and giving the results to the model.
- [Knowledge graphs and GraphRAG](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/techniques/knowledge-graphs.md): Storing facts as entities and relations, for questions that span several documents.
- [Memory](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/techniques/memory.md): Keeping information from one conversation to the next.
- [Prompt chaining](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/techniques/prompt-chaining.md): Splitting a task into steps, each with its own prompt.
- [Routing](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/techniques/routing.md): Sorting inputs and sending each one to the right prompt.
- [Parallel calls](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/techniques/parallelization.md): Running several prompts at once and combining the results.
- [Write and check](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/techniques/evaluator-optimizer.md): One prompt writes, another checks, and the loop repeats until the check passes.
- [Workflow graphs](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/techniques/workflow-graphs.md): Describing a workflow as steps and the connections between them.
- [Human approval](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/techniques/human-in-the-loop.md): Pausing for a person to approve or correct.
- [Function calling](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/techniques/function-calling.md): Letting the model call functions that you define.
- [Code execution](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/techniques/code-execution.md): Letting the model write code and run it in a sandbox.
- [Model Context Protocol](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/techniques/mcp.md): A standard way to connect models to tools and data.
- [Computer and browser use](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/techniques/computer-use.md): Letting the model operate a screen, a mouse and a keyboard.
- [Single agent](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/techniques/single-agent.md): A model that plans, acts and checks its own work in a loop.
- [The agent harness](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/techniques/agent-harness.md): Everything around the model in an agent: the loop, tools, context handling, permissions, caps and sandbox.
- [Agentic RAG and deep research](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/techniques/agentic-rag.md): An agent that runs its own searches until it has an answer.
- [Coding agents](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/techniques/coding-agents.md): Agents that read, write, run and test code.
- [Skills](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/techniques/skills.md): Reusable instructions that an agent loads when it needs them.
- [Voice agents](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/techniques/voice-agents.md): Agents you talk to in real time.
- [Lead agent and workers](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/techniques/orchestrator-workers.md): A lead agent splits the task and hands parts to other agents.
- [Agent graphs](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/techniques/agent-graphs.md): Describing a team of agents and how work passes between them.
- [Review and debate](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/techniques/debate-review.md): Agents that check, or argue with, each other's work.
- [Long-running tasks](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/techniques/long-horizon.md): Tasks that run for hours or days.
- [Always-on assistants](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/techniques/agent-teammates.md): Agents with their own computer that work without being asked.
- [Organizations of agents](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/techniques/organizations-swarms.md): Large groups of agents with roles and shared goals.
- [Robots and machines](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/techniques/embodied.md): Models that control robots and other machines.

## Topics
- [Topics at every level](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/levels/tracks/): Five topics that apply whichever level you use.
- [Evals](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/techniques/evals.md): Measuring whether a change made the results better.
- [Evaluation frameworks](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/techniques/eval-frameworks.md): The tools that run test sets and graders for you, and what to check before trusting their numbers.
- [Changing the model](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/techniques/adaptation.md): Fine-tuning, distillation, synthetic data and automated prompt tuning.
- [Fine-tuning and adapters](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/techniques/fine-tuning.md): Training a model further on your own examples, in full or with small adapters such as LoRA.
- [Distillation](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/techniques/distillation.md): Training a smaller model to reproduce what a larger one does on your task.
- [Synthetic data](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/techniques/synthetic-data.md): Using a model to write training or test examples, and checking them before they are used.
- [Prompt optimization](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/techniques/prompt-optimization.md): Letting a program search for better prompts against a test set.
- [Safety, privacy and governance](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/techniques/safety.md): Prompt injection, permissions, data handling and audit.
- [Guardrails](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/techniques/guardrails.md): Checks on what goes into a model and what comes out, and the limits of those checks.
- [Red teaming](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/techniques/red-teaming.md): Attacking your own system on purpose, before someone else does, and turning what you find into tests.
- [Operations](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/techniques/ops.md): Cost, speed, monitoring and running models on your own hardware.
- [Observability](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/techniques/observability.md): Recording what each run did, so a bad result can be traced to the step that caused it.
- [AI gateways](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/techniques/ai-gateways.md): One entry point in front of several model providers, for keys, routing, limits, fallback and logs.
- [Cost optimization](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/techniques/cost-optimization.md): Spending fewer tokens and less time for the same result: caching, batching, smaller models, shorter context.
- [Running models locally](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/techniques/local-inference.md): Running open-weight models on your own hardware: what fits, quantization, and what you give up.
- [Working with a model](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/techniques/operator-craft.md): How to brief a model, review its work and decide what to hand over.
- [Briefing: saying what you want](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/techniques/briefing.md): Saying what you want clearly enough that the model does not have to guess.
- [Reviewing work you did not do](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/techniques/reviewing.md): Checking work you did not do yourself before it goes anywhere.
- [Deciding what to hand over](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/techniques/delegating.md): Deciding which parts of a task to hand to a model and which to keep.
- [Calibrating trust](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/techniques/trust.md): Learning, from results over time, how much to rely on a model without checking.

## Threads
- [Graph engineering](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/threads/graph-engineering.md): Two uses of graphs that are often confused: graphs that connect information, and graphs that connect work. Knowledge graphs connect information; agent graphs connect work.
- [Who approves what](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/threads/who-approves-what.md): The same question asked at every level: which part of this does a person still decide? The answer moves from reading each result to setting the limits a run happens inside. A person never leaves; what they hold changes from the answer, to the action, to the rules the actions run under.
- [Checking the work](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/threads/checking-the-work.md): How you tell whether it worked, from a person reading one answer to a scored set and a recorded trace. The check changes shape at every level; the question does not. Every level has a way to be wrong that the level below could not be, and a check that costs less than the mistake.
- [What the model sees](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/threads/what-the-model-sees.md): One question followed across the site: what is in front of the model this turn, and who decided to put it there. The answers run from a written instruction to a note a session leaves for the next one. A model knows what it was trained on and what is in this request; everything else is a choice somebody made.

## Recipes
- [Answer questions about a set of documents](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/recipes/document-qa/): Uses RAG, structured output and an eval set. Level 2 is enough because a single search answers most questions. (this example uses level 2)
- [Sort an inbox](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/recipes/inbox-triage/): Sorts mail into fixed categories and produces structured output. A person approves anything that gets sent. The categories are known in advance, so an agent is not needed. (this example uses level 3)
- [Write a research brief with citations](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/recipes/research-brief/): Uses agentic RAG to find sources and a fixed check on every claim against the section it cites. It needs level 5 for the searching; the checking is level 3. (this example uses level 5)
- [Coding assistant on your own repo](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/recipes/repo-assistant/): A coding agent that reads, edits, runs and tests code in your repository, using skills for repeated tasks and a safety review before anything ships. (this example uses level 5)
- [Turn photos and PDFs into records](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/recipes/document-extraction/): Reads the image or PDF, fills a fixed schema, and saves the record once a person confirms it. (this example uses level 3)
- [Voice notes into structured entries](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/recipes/voice-notes/): Transcribes a voice note, splits it into steps, and turns each step into a structured entry that an eval set checks for accuracy. (this example uses level 3)
- [Support desk](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/recipes/support-desk/): Routes an incoming ticket, searches the documentation for an answer, calls a tool when an action is needed, and hands off to a person when it is unsure. (this example uses level 4)
- [Nightly source monitor](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/recipes/nightly-monitor/): Runs on a timer, diffs a set of public pages in code, and asks a model one question about each change. Level 3: the schedule and the checkpoint are infrastructure, not agency. (this example uses level 3)
- [Data analysis by conversation](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/recipes/data-analysis/): A single agent writes and runs code against a dataset, one question at a time, to answer questions a fixed query could not anticipate. (this example uses level 5)
- [Drafting with a reviewer](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/recipes/content-pipeline/): One prompt drafts a piece of writing and another checks it against a rubric, repeating until the draft passes. (this example uses level 3)
- [A team of personal assistants](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/recipes/assistant-team/): Several always-on agents split personal tasks among themselves, sharing memory and staying inside the same safety rules. (this example uses level 7)
- [Plain-language maintenance log](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/recipes/maintenance-log/): Turns a plain-language description of work done into a structured log entry, saved with a tool call and linked to the equipment it concerns through a small knowledge graph. (this example uses level 4)
- [Keep the household paperwork straight](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/recipes/household-paperwork/): Renewal dates, a naming rule for the folder, totals by category and a reminder before anything auto-renews. All of it is a sort, a date subtraction and a sum, so no model is involved anywhere. Level 0 is the whole recipe, and it is where most household admin actually lives; the one part that does need a model, reading a scanned bill, is its own recipe. (this example uses level 0)
- [Turn a meeting transcript into decisions and owners](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/recipes/meeting-notes/): One call turns a transcript into decisions, owners and open questions in a fixed shape, and somebody who was in the room reads it before it goes anywhere. Everything the job needs is already in the transcript, so level 1 is enough: the shape is what makes the output usable, not a workflow around it. (this example uses level 1)
- [Match invoices to purchase orders](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/recipes/invoice-matching/): The match itself is a join on a purchase-order number and three subtractions, which is level 0 and should stay there. A model only reads the invoice the supplier sent as a PDF into the fields the join needs, and anything that does not reconcile to the cent waits for a person. (this example uses level 3)
- [Check an agreement against your own checklist](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/recipes/contract-review/): One call per checklist item over the same agreement, each returning the clause it found and the rule that clause breaks, merged into one list a person reads. The checklist is written down in advance and does not change from one agreement to the next, which is what keeps this at level 3. (this example uses level 3)
- [Turn an incident write-up into a runbook](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/recipes/incident-runbook/): A fixed chain: pull the timeline out of the write-up, turn each action that would be done again into a numbered step, then check that every step names who does it and how to tell it worked. The person who ran the incident approves it before anyone follows it. The steps are known in advance, so level 3. (this example uses level 3)
- [Turn a script into a shot list](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/recipes/storyboard-from-a-script/): Scenes first, then shots inside each scene, then a check in code that every line of the script is covered by a shot and every shot points back at a line. A fixed three-step chain with a person reading the result, which is level 3. Drawing the frames is a different job and this recipe does not do it. (this example uses level 3)
- [Plan a trip and hold the bookings](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/recipes/trip-planning/): Checking what is available, what is open and what connects takes a different number of steps every time, which is what level 5 is for. Read-only lookups run unattended; anything that spends money stops for a person, with the price and the cancellation terms in front of them. (this example uses level 5)
- [Grade against a rubric, with a second reader](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/recipes/rubric-grading/): Two independent passes grade the same work against the same written rubric without seeing each other's scores, and every disagreement goes to the teacher instead of being averaged away. Level 6 earns its cost here because a wrong grade is expensive to the person who receives it, and an independent second reader is what catches a misread rule. (this example uses level 6)
- [Watch a topic for new work and summarize what turns up](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/recipes/literature-watch/): The site's first worked join of two job shapes, and still the simplest one. A standing weekly watch over a fixed list of sources works out in code which records are new, which is arithmetic and calls no model: level 0. Each new record then gets one call that turns its title and abstract into three sentences, with the citation attached by code from the source record and never written by the model: level 1. Neither half needs more, so the joined job settles at level 1, below where a watch usually lands. Deciding what to look for next, or following a reference to the next paper, would be level 5 research, and this is not that. (this example uses level 1)
- [Assemble a weekly status report from several systems](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/recipes/weekly-status-report/): The standing Friday report a small office runs on, pulled from a project tracker, a shared inbox and a spreadsheet. The assembly is level 0 and it is most of the job: pull three sources, reconcile the names they spell differently, and compute every count, date and total the report may quote. The writing is one call, level 1, handed those figures and nothing it could compute a number from. Two checks in code then read the draft in opposite directions, one for a number the model invented and one for a figure it left out, and a person reads it before it goes out. (this example uses level 1)
- [Keep a tracker document current from several sources](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/recipes/project-tracker-upkeep/): The other half of the same office's week, and a different job from writing a report: a report is read once, a tracker has to still be true next week. Code compares every field against the source that owns it and leaves most of the document alone. A model reads the shared inbox, one call per message, and proposes changes it can quote; none of them writes, because a fact read out of a sentence is a claim and not a record. A person approves anything that overwrites a field a person wrote, which is what makes the joined job level 3. The failure it is built around is absence: a source that goes quiet reads as nothing changed and quietly ages the whole document, so silence is detected and reported rather than assumed. (this example uses level 3)
- [Check measurements against limits, and chart what drifts](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/recipes/limits-without-a-model/): Limits, first-pass yield, Cpk, a control chart, and the same measurements grouped by lot, by fixture, by day and by shift. No model is involved anywhere, and the pass or fail decision never should be: a wrong pass ships a bad unit. Level 0 is the whole recipe, and most of a test engineer's week is this. (this example uses level 0)
- [Sweep a design over its corners and report the margins](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/recipes/characterize-a-design/): Five prototype boards, a sweep over line, load and temperature, the margin to every datasheet limit at every corner, the uncertainty budget behind each margin and the guardbanded verdict that follows from it. All of it is arithmetic: a sweep is a loop, a margin is a subtraction, a budget is a root sum of squares. The engineering-test counterpart to the production limits recipe, and level 0 is the whole recipe. This is where the numbers in a design review report come from. (this example uses level 0)
- [Turn a measurement session into a report somebody can review](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/recipes/measurement-writeup/): The notebook and the computed results become a characterization report a reviewer can read, which is what most people mean by writing up a design review. Code computes every number and places it; the model writes the prose around the numbers and never touches them; a check in code confirms that every figure in the draft is one code produced; a person reads it before it goes out. One call, so level 1, and the check is what makes the call safe to make. (this example uses level 1)
- [Answer questions from a datasheet, a test spec and a change notice](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/recipes/ask-the-datasheet/): Retrieval over the documents an engineer already has, answered with citations that can be checked. The case that matters is a change notice contradicting the datasheet on one number, where the right answer depends on the board revision. Level 2 is enough because one search finds the passage. (this example uses level 2)
- [Pull an instrument's accuracy table out of its manual](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/recipes/accuracy-specs-from-the-manual/): The model reads a programming manual and fills a schema: one row per range per calibration interval, ppm of reading and ppm of range, the temperature band and the coefficient outside it. Code validates the rows and computes the budget from them, and a person checks every row against the manual before anything is quoted from it. The case that matters is a right-looking number from the wrong interval or the wrong range. (this example uses level 3)
- [Sort failing units and operator notes into causes](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/recipes/test-failure-triage/): Failing measurements and free-text operator notes are sorted into the causes the failure analysis guide already lists, then routed. A person confirms before anything is scrapped or reworked. The categories are known in advance, so this is classification into fixed classes and not an agent. (this example uses level 3)
- [Check a board against the design rules document](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/recipes/design-review-checklist/): A bill of materials and a netlist summary are checked rule by rule against the written design rules. One pass drafts findings, a second checks each finding against the rule text it cites and drops the ones that cite nothing. Level 3, because code decides every step and the rules do not change between boards. This is the rule check that happens before a review meeting, not the design review report itself: for the report, and the characterization data behind it, see the two recipes this page links in its first paragraph. (this example uses level 3)
- [Turn a requirements list into a test plan](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/recipes/requirements-to-test-plan/): A fixed chain: read the requirements, propose a test for each, build the traceability table, then check that every requirement has a test and every test names a requirement. A person approves before any of it is adopted. The order of the steps is known in advance, which is what keeps this at level 3. (this example uses level 3)
- [Draft an instrument control script from its programming manual](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/recipes/instrument-script-from-the-manual/): The model drafts commands from the manual for that instrument; code checks every one against the documented command set, runs the script on the simulated instrument, and feeds the errors back for another pass. A person bench-checks before it drives real hardware, and every set point goes through a code-side envelope. (this example uses level 4)
- [Ask questions of a production test log](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/recipes/test-data-by-conversation/): Starts where the dashboard stopped: limits, yield and Cpk are already charted and did not answer the question. The model writes analysis code that runs in a sandbox over the CSV, and a person reads the code as well as the answer. Includes the trap of a column in millivolts under a header that says volts. (this example uses level 4)
- [Work a bring-up problem at the bench](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/recipes/bring-up-debug-assistant/): An agent with read-only tools, instrument queries, the test log and the datasheet, works a low output down to a cause and proposes the next measurement. Queries run unattended; anything that sets a voltage, a current limit or an output goes through the envelope and a person. Level 5 because each measurement depends on the last. (this example uses level 5)

## Teardowns

- [A coding agent, decoded](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/teardowns/coding-agent/): one kind of product decoded into agent-harness, single-agent, coding-agents, skills, orchestrator-workers, safety (reviewed 2026-09-18, expires 2027-03-17).
- [An always-on agent teammate, decoded](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/teardowns/agent-teammate/): one kind of product decoded into agent-teammates, long-horizon, computer-use, human-in-the-loop (reviewed 2026-09-18, expires 2027-03-17).
- [A search-grounded answer engine, decoded](https://reedos.github.io/gradient_ascent/teardowns/answer-engine/): one kind of product decoded into rag, context-engineering, routing (reviewed 2026-09-19, expires 2027-03-18).
